newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-MARTINEZ AND MOYA LOOK TO ADD TO SPAIN'S SUCCESS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MARTINEZ AND MOYA LOOK TO ADD TO SPAIN'S SUCCESS.

text.p: Third seed Conchita Martinez and giant-killer Carlos Moya can add to Spain's early successes at the Australian Open when the second round begins on Wednesday.
All five of Spain's seeded players, part of a 23-strong contingent renowned for their clay court expertise, survived the first round on the faster Rebound Ace surface.
But it was unseeded Moya who created the major upset of the tournament when he defeated reigning champion and sixth seed Boris Becker of Germany on Monday.
Moya's reward is an encounter with another unseeded player, American Patrick McEnroe.

Martinez, the Wimbledon champion in 1994, reached the semifinals at the Australian Open the following year in her best result to date in Melbourne. She will meet Adriana Gersi of the Czech Republic on court one.

Women's second seed Arantxa Sanchez Vicario and men's 10th seed Albert Costa added their weight to the Spanish charge with straight sets victories over Italy's Gloria Pizzichini and Australian Patrick Rafter respectively on Tuesday night.
Unseeded Sergi Bruguera, a former French Open champion, takes on Swede Magnus Larsson, while compatriot Felix Mantilla, seeded 14, will tackle Brazil's Fernando Meligeni.
Wednesday will also see second seed Michael Chang seeking to avenge a defeat by fellow American Richey Reneberg and top seed Steffi Graf hoping for her first full match.
Chang breezed through to the second round, losing only four games to Kris Goossens of Belgium on Monday, but knows he faces a much tougher opponent in Reneberg, ranked 31st in the world.
Graf spent only 21 minutes on court on Monday before her opponent, Jannette Husarova of Slovakia, forfeited the match due to a knee injury while trailing the world number one 5-1.
